doc.title: Norris Turney interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Leaving for Jeter Pillars, Tiny Bradshaw and Eckstine
summary: After a year at the Cotton Club he joined Jeter Pillars in St. Louis, then Tiny Bradshaw, then Billy Eckstine, before going home.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Gee by the mid 40s then you started playing with some fairly well known names: Tiny Bradshaw and was this road work?
It was like time to leave home and go out?
Yeah, well, I’d been working at the Cotton Club for maybe a year or so, and I left there and went to St. Louis when I joined the Jeter Pillars Orchestra. You ever heard of them?

Very good. Excellent. And I worked with Jeter I guess about a year. And then I left him and went to join Tiny Bradshaw. And after Tiny Bradshaw I joined Billy Eckstine’s band. And that was the end of my road work for a while, I went back home.
